Sheet pinned beside the tide tables in the Torvig harbour office. Transcribed
rather than read by OCR: it is boxes, bars and labels, and a column-wise reading
turns it into word salad.

**Title:** The rule of twelfths. **Subtitle:** How the range is distributed over
the six hours of the flood.

Three boxes across the top, left to right:

- *Hour 1 + 2* — one twelfth and two twelfths of the range; the water barely
  moves.
- *Hour 3 + 4* — three twelfths each; half the range is passed after hour three.
- *Hour 5 + 6* — two twelfths and one twelfth; the rise runs out towards high
  water.

Below them a bar chart, six bars, one per hour, heights in the same proportion:
1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1. Each bar is labelled with its fraction above and its hour
below. A rule runs under the bars from "Low water" on the left to "High water"
on the right, with "six hours" written along it.

![Figure: How the tidal range is spread over the six hours between low and high water](figures/island-images/tide-chart.svg)

Footnote, set small and italic: Torvig Harbour — mean range 3.4 m, springs
5.1 m, neaps 1.7 m.
